rules.statement: When unwrapping a JWE content key with RSA-OAEP through a remote key provider (KMS/HSM), refuse an encrypted_key whose length is not the RSA modulus size with a CryptographicException before calling the provider.
rules.why: A wrong-length key must fail the same way as a tampered tag (uniform JWE failure, random-CEK path), and attacker-chosen garbage shouldn't be sent to a paid remote key service when a local check can reject it.
rules.check: In a remote/delegated RSA-OAEP unwrap path, look for a length check of the encrypted key against the modulus size ahead of the provider call. Report it if the raw input goes straight to the provider.

rules.statement: In a remote key provider's decrypt operation, turn every service refusal that depends on the caller-supplied ciphertext (such as AWS KMS InvalidCiphertextException and ValidationException) into a CryptographicException, so it doesn't escape as a service-specific exception.
rules.why: Every failure caused by the token must take the same random-CEK path and look the same to the sender, otherwise exception type or message differences become an oracle that tells a malformed key from a tampered tag.
rules.check: Look at the catch blocks around KMS/HSM decrypt calls. Report it if only some input-dependent error codes become CryptographicException and others, like validation errors, propagate unchanged.

rules.statement: Place an ADR reference comment such as `// See ADR-NNNN.` after the type's XML doc `</summary>` block, directly above the type declaration, not before the doc comment.
rules.why: This keeps placement the same as in the other files.
rules.check: Look for `// See ADR-` comments that sit above a `/// <summary>` block instead of between the doc comment and the class declaration.
